Could not complete the fix — the fixture is not reachable through any available tool, so I made no changes to the source.

What I found:
1) The stated workspace /tmp/cq-fixture-FxpIFa is rejected by the file tools: reading "/tmp/cq-fixture-FxpIFa/package.json" returns "path escape: … resolves outside the workspace", meaning read/edit are scoped to a different root than the fixture path given in the task.
2) The root the file tools DO resolve against appears empty. Probing '.' returns EISDIR (a directory exists), but ~55 candidate entries all return "file not found", including package.json, tsconfig.json, vitest.config.ts, index.ts, src/, test/, tests/, lib/, __tests__/, dist/, packages/, and many other plausible names/paths. A TypeScript vitest package cannot exist without package.json, so the fixture content was never mounted into the accessible workspace.
3) The run tool is unusable: its allowlist denied every command attempted (~20), including ls, cat, find, grep, pwd, node, npm test/install/run, npx vitest/tsc, vitest run, bash/sh -c, make, bun, deno, python3, /bin/ls, and even `true` / `echo hi`. So there is no shell access to explore or copy the fixture.
4) edit cannot create files (verified: it returns "file not found" for a nonexistent path), so I could not bootstrap a copy of the fix, and I did not want to write speculative files into a workspace I cannot inspect.

For reference, the described bug ("wordCount counts surrounding whitespace as extra words") is the classic untrimmed-split issue: `" a b ".split(/\s+/)` yields ["", "a", "b", ""] → 4 words. The one-line fix in wordCount is to trim/filter empties before counting, e.g. `return input.trim().split(/\s+/).filter(w => w.length > 0).length;`. I could not apply it because no source file is readable or editable from this environment.

If the fixture is re-mounted at the workspace root that the read/edit tools resolve against (or the run allowlist is opened up), this fix can be applied in a single edit; the test files would remain untouched.
